native_mechanisms: Placing a stone on a corner finalises its distance, never reconsidered afterwards (settled/permanent-label set)
A duck carries a spooled thread whose length is the running sum of road centimetres traversed to reach it (tentative distance labels, relaxed by addition)

Each round, exhaustively compare threads to find the single leader duck with the shortest carried length among unstoned corners, and settle it before any other duck moves (linear scan extract-min, full pass with no early exit)
Slack roads toward dead-end houses (no outgoing side) are discarded unspooled and never measured again (pruning edges into sink vertices)
Discard a freshly laid thread unless its sum beats the thread the far corner already wears (relaxation test / no-improvement discard)
Corners the ducks never reach stay bare — unreachable vertices keep infinite/absent distance
core_technique: Dijkstra's algorithm with a compacted frontier array and AVX2-vectorised linear extract-min scan (the classic O(n^2)-style array-scan variant), adaptively switching to a binary-heap Dijkstra mid-run when measured scan cost exceeds a degree/log-n threshold; CSR edge layout and a Bellman-Ford fallback on allocation failure.
